title: One payment, six models
description: Teaching case: asynchronous confirmation reveals stale assumptions across separate diagrams. Tags retain original model roles; the current renderer uses Plyra cards.

nodes.name: Accept order
nodes.body:
A process task. Accepts an order without declaring it paid.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Request payment
nodes.body:
Process activity implemented by Payment API. Its ID is distinct from the application's ID.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Release for shipping
nodes.body:
The old process releases an order after the request returns. Review the confirmation condition when the provider changes.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Payment API
nodes.body:
Python application; calls the provider over HTTPS. Asynchronous confirmation needs an event receiver and duplicate-event protection.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Payment provider
nodes.body:
Fictional change: confirmation arrives as an event within 15 minutes. An accepted request is not a successful payment.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Payment
nodes.body:
One classifier appears in the class view and as the state machine context. Fields: id, status, providerEventId. Paid is a separate state entity.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Created
nodes.body:
Created. The old state machine does not represent waiting for provider confirmation.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Paid
nodes.body:
Enter this state only after confirmed success, not upon 202 Accepted.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: REQ-17 · ship only after confirmation
nodes.body:
This requirement connects the process, architecture and test. Its appearances share an ID; the activity, service and test keep their own IDs.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: REQ-18 · apply an event once
nodes.body:
A repeated event must not release the order twice. Delivery may repeat; the requirement concerns the processing effect.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Duplicate-event test
nodes.body:
Send the same event twice, then a late confirmation after timeout. Check the final status and number of releases.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Shipping an unpaid order
nodes.body:
Cause: synchronous response assumptions applied to an asynchronous contract. Controls: verify confirmation and test late responses.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.

nodes.name: Duplicate shipment
nodes.body:
A repeated event repeats a business effect. Controls: idempotency key, atomic handling and duplicate-event test.

Source: fictional Plyra teaching scenario. This is a traceability map, not an executable model.
